newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila firm buys 17,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat.
newsitem.headline: Manila firm buys 17,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat.

text.p: A Philippine food manufacturer and flour miller bought 17,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat for mid-November shipment, traders said on Friday.
The firm also bought 6,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans at over $200 per tonne FOB from an American commodity house Thursday night, they said.

Traders said the firm bought 11,000 tonnes of dark northern spring wheat with a 13.5 percent protein content at $4.10 per bushel FOB, and another 6,000 tonnes of western white wheat at $4.0 per bushel FOB.
Another Philippine flour miller had invited tenders earlier today for 12,000 tonnes of combined U.S. dark northern spring wheat and western white wheat, traders said.
"The tenders will be opened at 4 p.m. (0800 GMT)," one trader who joined the bidding said.
"The two Philippine firms planned to share shipping cost for their commodity orders," the same trader said.
Traders said the two Philippine firms planned to invite shipping companies to bid for the shipment of their orders on October 28.
